🧄 When to plant garlic in Nigeria

Also called Tafarnuwa (Hausa) and Ayu (Yoruba).

Quick answer: Plant garlic in Nigeria from October to November and harvest from February to March. Cloves are planted October–November in the cool dry season; harvested February–March.

PlantOctober to November
HarvestFebruary to March
Grows inNorth-West and North-Central
TypeFruit vegetables
Local namesTafarnuwa · Ayu
JanFebMarAprMayJunJulAugSepOctNovDec

■ plant   ■ harvest

About garlic

Garlic needs cool Harmattan nights to form good bulbs.

How to plant garlic well

Plant individual cloves, pointed end up.

Cloves are planted October–November in the cool dry season; harvested February–March.

Diseases and pests of garlic

  • White rotRotate fields; don't replant garlic or onion on the same land soon.
  • Purple blotchUse recommended fungicides and good spacing.

Best states for garlic

Kano · Katsina · Plateau · Kaduna · Jigawa · Sokoto

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant garlic in Nigeria?

Plant garlic in Nigeria from October to November and harvest from February to March. Cloves are planted October–November in the cool dry season; harvested February–March.

What is garlic called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Garlic is called Tafarnuwa (Hausa) and Ayu (Yoruba).

When is garlic harvested in Nigeria?

Garlic is usually harvested from February to March.

Which Nigerian states grow the most garlic?

Kano, Katsina, Plateau, Kaduna, Jigawa and Sokoto are among the best-known garlic states.

Can I grow garlic in my part of Nigeria?

Garlic grows best in the North-West and North-Central regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack garlic and how do I prevent them?

White rot: Rotate fields; don't replant garlic or onion on the same land soon. Purple blotch: Use recommended fungicides and good spacing.
